title: Why New Year Resolutions Fail Without Character We are one week into the New Year and most of us are probably sticking to our resolutions
author: Chris Martin
source: The Ways of a Gentleman (Martin Substack), January 8, 2026
summary: Martin observes that New Year's resolutions fail in overwhelming numbers not because the goals are unrealistic but because people attempt to achieve them without building the character necessary to sustain the effort. A resolution to exercise, eat healthily, or read more requires discipline, persistence, and the ability to delay gratification—all character traits that cannot be developed in a moment but must be cultivated over time. Martin argues that before making resolutions, people would be better served developing the character foundations: consistency in small things, follow-through on commitments, and the ability to endure discomfort for long-term gain. Character is the prerequisite for meaningful change, not the result of it. Those who succeed at sustained change are typically those who have already developed the character to sustain habits—the resolution is simply an application of existing strength.
points: New Year's resolutions fail in overwhelming numbers not because goals are unrealistic but because people attempt them without the character necessary to sustain effort.
A resolution to change requires character traits like discipline, persistence, and the ability to delay gratification—these cannot be developed in a moment but must be cultivated over time.
Before making resolutions, people would benefit more from developing character foundations: consistency in small things, follow-through on commitments, and ability to endure discomfort.
Character is the prerequisite for meaningful change, not the result of it—those who succeed have typically already developed the character strength to sustain new habits.
The resolution is simply an application of existing character strength; without that foundation, even well-intentioned goals collapse under the first real pressure or setback.
